text:
Justin Brazeau has played seven games for Pittsburgh this season, and the role has shrunk to about ten minutes a night. He has one goal, scored against his old team, Boston, on Nov 5, in his best game of the year (four shots).

It's a strange fit for a player whose game is getting to the net. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at the 99th percentile among forwards last season for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net, and 21% of his setups came from behind the goal line, against 8% for a typical forward. That's a power forward's toolkit, and Evolving-Hockey valued it at 1.1 wins last season.

This season the on-ice numbers have been rough in a small sample: Pittsburgh gets 40% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, 13 points worse than without him. His talent range puts his scoring rate well above where he's running.

He last played on Nov 19. What to watch: whether he gets back into the lineup, and in a role that puts him near the crease, where his game lives.
